messages:
maya: Heads up — since ~09:12UTC we're seeing apiserver 502/504 spikes in eu-central1. controller-manager leader flips ~6x, etcd follower-2 lagging ~30s. Coincides with the GPU provisioning batch job that kicked off at 09:10 (400 nodes).

andre: :eyes: can you paste the apiserver error snippets / prometheus panels?

maya: quick slices: 
- apiserver errors: `apiserver_request_duration_seconds_bucket{code="502"}` spike from 0 -> 600 qps
- etcd: `etcd_server_proposals_failed_total` increased, follower-2 `apply_latency` ~700ms
- watch events backlog: `apiserver_watch_event_backlog` ~1200

sylvia: Any network egress or node-setup hooks hammering control plane? The GPU bootstrap runs container image pulls + nvdriver init which does a lot of CNI + kubelet registration chatter.

maya: Exactly. I correlated flow logs — nodes in the new pool saturated egress path to the controlplane subnet (~60% packet loss spikes for short windows). That led to etcd heartbeats missing and controller-manager leader election churn.

liam: ops-bot created an incident: `INC-3456` with initial severity P1 (auto) — tagging on-call.

ops-bot: Incident INC-3456 created. On-call: liam.

andre: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) pause/slow provisioning job 2) cordon newly created GPU nodes 3) apply k8s apiserver rate-limiting/burst tweaks temporarily 4) prioritize controlplane traffic (policy/QoS) on the egress LB.

sylvia: I'm running `kubectl cordon` on the new pool nodes now and scaling the provisioner back to 25%. Also bumping kube-proxy conntrack timeout? Not yet.

maya: Thanks — after cordon + scaleback, apiserver 502s dropped to baseline within 3m, election flaps decreased. Current watch backlog down to ~200 and etcd follower apply_latency back to ~50ms.

liam: Nice. For longer term: we should add rate-limit to the node bootstrap path and move heavy image pulls to a regional artifact mirror to reduce egress bursts. Also consider decoupling GPU driver init from node registration (register node after image+driver ready).

andre: Agreed. Also file: increase etcd follower election timeout a hair for high-churn windows (but document carefully). And add a preflight that warns if provisioning rate > X nodes/min per region when controlplane egress util > Y%.

maya: I'll open a post-incident RFC with proposed changes: - provisioner rate limiting + leaky-bucket - node-bootstrap deferred registration flow - QoS on controlplane LB - observability: synthetic leader-election test + watch-lag alerting thresholds.

sylvia: For cost note: the provisioner was trying to grab cheaper preemptible GPU capacity in the same region which led to a concentrated burst. Spreading across zones or opportunistic across regions would reduce blasting single controlplane link but could increase egress costs. We should quantify tradeoffs.

liam: For now, leave the new nodes cordoned for 2 hours. We'll gradually uncordon 50 nodes at a time via the reduced-rate provisioner job. Notify when you start uncordoning.

maya: Will do. Starting staged uncordon at 09:42 UTC (50 nodes). Will report metrics after each batch.

deploy-bot: Scheduled job `gpu-provisioner` paused by sylvia at 09:15 UTC.

maya: Update: after two batches uncordoned apiserver errors remain low, watch backlog ~80. Marking INC-3456 as monitoring.

andre: Please include the exact egress interface / firewall rule we hit so infra can provision dedicated controlplane egress bandwidth or QoS.

maya: Logged infra ticket INFRA-789 with flow logs, capturing 3 short saturation windows on `eu-central1-egress-01`.

liam: Great postmortem inputs. sylvia/maya — can you draft the short blameless postmortem and the actionable runbook items? I'll set follow-ups for infra + provisioner team next week. :thumbsup:
